analysis.title: CoreWeave Inc (CRWV US) Reduce: Bullish pricing comments need careful evaluation
key_insights: 3Q26 revenue was USD3,661m, 2.9% above consensus of USD3,557m and in line with HSBCe of USD3,663m. HSBC says the slight beat versus consensus seems driven by higher-than-expected, and guided, capex.

3Q26 non-GAAP operating margin was 10.4% versus HSBCe 8.0%, consensus 6.9% and guidance 6.5%. HSBC does not read much into the beat because consensus and HSBC estimates were pulled down by overly conservative guidance. TTM non-GAAP operating margin is about 5.5%, versus a c16% average before the dip. HSBC expects margins to normalize near 16%.

CoreWeave said it can sell compute capacity at USD20-25m per annum per MW on four- to five-year contracts, and up to USD40m on short-term contracts. HSBC estimates the company has historically realized USD12-13m per annum per MW.
HSBC reads the pricing comments as either excessive optimism or higher cost capacity per MW than in the past. It does not see runaway pricing.

Asset turnover (annualized revenue / gross PP&E excluding construction in progress and operating leases) was 30.5% in 3Q26, versus 28.6% in 2Q26, 30.0% in 2025 and 34.8% in 2024. Exit-2026 ARR guidance of USD20-21bn (raised from USD18.5-19.5bn), read with 4Q26 capex guidance, implies exit asset turnover of about 32.6%. HSBC models about 33% medium term.

On a historical rule of thumb of about USD50bn capex per GW, with USD37.5bn on IT equipment, 33% asset turnover implies about USD12.4m per annum per MW. CoreWeave's asset turnover trend is similar to Oracle OCI and Microsoft Azure.

CoreWeave guided 2027 non-GAAP EBITDA/interest expense (excluding prepayments) to 'more than double' year on year. HSBC and consensus model 2.4-2.6x, so HSBC says the comment could be read as conservative or disappointing. HSBC would have preferred an explicit 'more than 2.5x' if management expects that. Full 2027 guidance is likely with 4Q26 results.
The company expects positive non-GAAP net profit in 1H28. Consensus is USD85m and HSBC USD82m.
The company expects to collect about USD9bn of prepayments and deposits from signed customer contracts in 4Q26. HSBC believes these advances are interest bearing, as at Oracle.

Undrawn credit facilities fell to USD5bn in 3Q26 from USD10bn in 2Q26. Cash including financial investments was USD6,466m versus USD6,919m in 2Q26. HSBC estimates CoreWeave needs to raise USD33bn of fresh financing in 2027.

HSBC does not see a clear pivot to short-term contracts. The share of total RPO due within 24 months fell to 36% in 3Q26 from 41% in 2Q26, and total RPO rose to USD132.5bn from USD103.7bn. HSBC says this points to a more long-term-heavy order book.
3Q26 capex was USD14.5bn, 43.3% above HSBCe, 16.0% above consensus and 16% above guidance of USD12.5bn. Net debt was USD41,056m, 12.4% above consensus.

New guidance for 2026: revenue USD13.15bn (old USD12.8bn), non-GAAP operating profit USD1,325m (old USD1,055m), capex USD38bn (old USD37bn). 4Q26 guidance: revenue USD4,836m, non-GAAP operating profit USD797m, capex USD7,362m.

HSBC raised 2026e non-GAAP EPS to -USD3.59 from -USD3.93 and 2027e to -USD1.76 from -USD1.89. It cut 2028e to USD0.82 from USD0.96. Long-term non-GAAP EPS is little changed. Long-term capex, net debt and revenue estimates rise on stronger RPO growth, and interest cost assumptions rise on higher debt and customer financing.

CRWV trades at 11.7x 2030e non-GAAP EV/EBIT after SBC, versus 6.6x for Oracle and a slight premium to Amazon (9.2x), Microsoft (10.5x) and Meta (10.3x). HSBC calls the shares expensive despite the recent sell-off.

HSBC maintains Reduce with a DCF-based target price of USD39, unchanged, implying 20.0% downside from USD48.73 (10 Nov 2026 close). DCF inputs: cost of equity 11.5%, beta 1.80, risk-free rate 4.25%, market risk premium 4.0%, pre-tax cost of debt 10%, WACC 9.7%. The TP implies a CY28e non-GAAP PE of 48x, versus 46x on consensus.

market_movers.rationale: HSBC keeps Reduce and its USD39 DCF-based target after 3Q26 results, which beat conservative guidance. It calls the valuation expensive at 11.7x 2030e EV/EBIT versus 6.6x for Oracle and reads the pricing comments as excessive optimism or higher cost capacity.

earnings_insights: CRWV 3Q26 (reported, non-GAAP): revenue USD3,661m versus consensus USD3,557m, HSBCe USD3,663m and guidance USD3,525m. Non-GAAP operating profit was USD379m versus consensus USD245m and guidance USD230m. Non-GAAP EPS was -USD0.95 versus consensus -USD1.20 and HSBCe -USD1.07.

CRWV 3Q26 (reported, non-GAAP): EBITDA was USD2,256m (61.6% margin) versus consensus USD2,054m (57.7%) and HSBCe USD2,121m (57.9%). Capex was USD14.5bn versus consensus USD11.9bn and guidance USD12.5bn.

CRWV new guidance (company): 2026 revenue USD13.15bn (previously USD12.8bn, pre-results consensus USD12.91bn). 2026 non-GAAP operating profit USD1,325m (previously USD1,055m, consensus USD1,069m). 4Q26 revenue USD4,836m versus pre-results consensus USD4,720m. 4Q26 operating profit USD797m versus consensus USD676m.
CRWV 2026 capex guidance is USD38bn (previously USD37bn, pre-results consensus USD35.5bn). 4Q26 capex guidance is USD7,362m versus pre-results consensus USD9,479m.

HSBC estimate changes (HSBCe, not reported): 2026e non-GAAP EPS -USD3.59 (previously -USD3.93, consensus -USD3.79). 2027e -USD1.76 (previously -USD1.89, consensus -USD1.99). 2028e USD0.82 (previously USD0.96, consensus USD0.95). 2026e revenue USD13,145m (+1.3%) and 2027e USD27,887m (-2.6%).
risk_factors: Liquidity: undrawn credit facilities fell to USD5bn from USD10bn and HSBC estimates USD33bn of fresh financing is needed in 2027.
Re-leasing risk if the order book shifts to shorter contracts, though HSBC does not see that shift in RPO.
Leverage: net debt was USD41.1bn in 3Q26, HSBC forecasts USD64.4bn by 2027e, and 2027e free cash flow is deeply negative.
Upside risks to the Reduce call, per HSBC: better contract terms, stronger demand for GPU-focused clouds, lower competition, and better macro and financial conditions.

tension_points.bull_case: Management says it can sell capacity at USD20-25m per MW per annum on four- to five-year contracts and up to USD40m on short-term contracts, far above the roughly USD12-13m HSBC estimates was realized historically. Exit-2026 ARR guidance was raised to USD20-21bn.
tension_points.bear_case: HSBC says asset turnover of 30.5% in 3Q26 is in line with history and peers, so the comments indicate either excessive optimism or higher cost capacity per MW. It sees no runaway pricing and no clear shift to short-term contracts.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A move of asset turnover materially above the historical range of about 30-35%, or a rising share of RPO due within 24 months, which was 36% in 3Q26.

theme_stances.key_argument: Asset turnover is in line with history, so the pricing comments are either too optimistic or reflect higher capex per unit of capacity, and the valuation is expensive.
theme_stances.evidence: we conclude that the pricing comments are either too optimistic
